title: references/rest-channel.md header quotes a stale default read order — it omits the zero-quota payload tier that a 403-gated seat needs most
body:
Found while landing an unrelated fact row in `references/platform-readings.md`. Filed
unassigned, not fixed in that PR — different defect class, and the target file is a
separate governed surface at zero ratchet headroom.

## The drift

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/rest-channel.md` opens by naming its own source and
quoting the policy that lives there:

```text
出处:`platform-readings.md` API 配额段(**默认读序 git → REST → MCP/GraphQL** 的策略住那里,本表是
逐操作的通道归属)。
```

The source it names says something else. `references/platform-readings.md` carries:

```text
- **默认读序 git → payload → REST → MCP/GraphQL**(2026-08-23 策略翻转,2026-08-25 增补 payload 档;
```

The `payload` tier was added 2026-08-25 and the quoting header was never moved with it.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a shrug

The omitted tier is the **zero-quota public-repo payload channel**, and it sits in the read
order specifically *above* REST. The population that needs it is the seat whose repo-scoped
REST probe comes back 403 — which is measured to be a large share of container dev seats,
and for whom the header's three-step order silently degrades to "git, then MCP/GraphQL",
skipping the one tier that costs no quota at all.

The failure direction is the bad one: a header that under-states the ladder reads as
authoritative because it cites its source by name, so a seat that consults it has no cue to
go check the source. This was verified live on this very seat today — the probe returned
403 with `GitHub access is not enabled for this session`, and the payload channel is what
served the label reads afterwards.

## Fix shape, and the constraint on it

Roughly a one-token insertion into the quoted order. But note before dispatching:

- `rest-channel.md` is on the ratchet at **87 lines, ceiling 87, headroom 0**, so this must
  land net 0.
- Its line 3 is already **118 bytes** against the 120-byte cap, so the inserted word forces
  a re-wrap of that paragraph. The paragraph may absorb it without gaining a line — that is
  a measurement to make, not to assume.

Worth checking in the same stroke whether any other file quotes the read order and drifted
the same way; this one was found by reading, not by a gate, and nothing mechanically holds a
quoted policy equal to its source across these two files.
